name: CroissantMiner Benchmark
description: A benchmark for evaluating automated metadata extraction from ML dataset papers. Contains 8 academic papers with 30-field human-annotated ground truth following the MLCommons Croissant RAI schema. Includes extraction results from Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and GPT-4o-mini, plus ablation experiment data across prompt, context, and few-shot dimensions.
rai:dataCollection: Ground truth annotations were collected through a structured annotation study with 17 annotators (Phase 1 pilot) across academic institutions. Annotators verified AI-extracted metadata against original papers using TRUE/FALSE verdicts and provided corrections.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each annotator was assigned 3 metadata fields and 5 datasets. They compared AI-extracted values against the original paper and marked each as TRUE (correct) or FALSE (incorrect), providing corrected values and confidence levels.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom Excel annotation sheets generated by CroissantMiner annotation pipeline
rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 (double annotation for inter-annotator agreement on overlapping fields)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is versioned and maintained alongside the CroissantMiner tool. Phase 2 annotations (50 datasets, 5-point Likert scale) planned for v2.0.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is biased toward well-documented, English-language ML papers from major conferences. Papers with poor documentation quality tend to have lower extraction accuracy.
rai:dataLimitations: Limited to 8 benchmark datasets in v1.0. Ground truth for 14 RAI fields was initially generated by Claude and needs human verification. Binary TRUE/FALSE annotation scale in Phase 1 produced near-zero inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss' kappa = 0.005).
